items.q: In the anatomical schematic of the intrinsic laryngeal framework, which muscle is the SOLE abductor of the vocal cords responsible for opening the rima glottidis?
items.exp: The posterior cricoarytenoid is the sole abductor of the vocal folds. It originates from the posterior surface of the cricoid lamina and inserts into the muscular process of the arytenoid cartilage. Bilateral injury to the recurrent laryngeal nerves denervates this muscle, leading to unopposed adduction and life-threatening airway compromise.
r: Incorrect. Lateral cricoarytenoid is a major adductor.
Correct. Posterior cricoarytenoid is the only abductor of the vocal cords.
Incorrect. Cricothyroid elongates and tenses the vocal folds.
Incorrect. Thyroarytenoid relaxes the vocal ligaments.
items.kp: Posterior cricoarytenoid is the sole vocal cord abductor; bilateral denervation causes acute airway obstruction.

items.q: During thyroid surgery, ligation of the superior thyroid artery close to the superior pole of the thyroid gland risks injury to which accompanying nerve?
o: External branch of superior laryngeal nerve
Internal branch of superior laryngeal nerve
items.exp: The external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve descends in close proximity to the superior thyroid artery near the superior pole of the thyroid. It innervates the cricothyroid muscle. Injury impairs vocal cord tension, causing vocal fatigue, voice weakness, and inability to produce high-pitched sounds.
r: Incorrect. Recurrent laryngeal nerve is intimate with the inferior thyroid artery.
Correct. The external branch of superior laryngeal nerve travels alongside the superior thyroid artery.
Incorrect. Internal branch pierces the thyrohyoid membrane superiorly.
Incorrect. Ansa cervicalis lies superficial in the carotid sheath.
items.kp: External branch of superior laryngeal nerve accompanies superior thyroid artery; injury impairs high-pitch phonation.
